title: The Slope Where Falling Becomes Climbing Backward

features.name: the point of inversion
features.desc-on-touch: The slope steepens here, and something peculiar happens: things falling seem to slow, and things climbing seem to accelerate, and you cannot tell which way is down anymore.

features.name: a tree that fell upward
features.desc-on-touch: Its roots point to sky. The wood remembers the earth it came from, still reaching for the ground through the canopy.

features.name: time's shadow
features.desc-on-touch: An outline on the bark where past-tense used to rest. Now it moves with the slope, ascending and descending at once.

features.name: the two-direction path
features.desc-on-touch: Footprints here run both up and down simultaneously, leading nowhere twice.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the slope where time forgets which way it goes
narr: You stand on the slope and she stands on the slope, and the
trees fall both ways at once. She says: I thought the mesh was
ending. You say: No. It is still arriving. The leaves fall upward
in the dusk, and both of you understand: ending is the place
where continuing learns to breathe. The slope holds you both.

inscription: here even gravity argues with itself about which way is down

file.name: Palimpsest_of_Descent_and_Climbing_Comparative.mp3
file.note: A two-track recording where ascending and descending are the same sound played at different speeds; both directions coexist in the same moment
